newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan, India agree to free detained fishermen.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan, India agree to free detained fishermen.

text.p: Pakistan and India announced on Monday that they would free 389 fishermen and 61 boats identified as being held by each side by July 15.

"Pursuant to the decision of the prime ministers of Pakistan and India to exchange fishing boats and crew presently in the custody of either side, the matter was discussed in detail during the foreign secretary-level talks," a joint statement said.
"The two sides have now verified 26 Pakistani boats and 195 crew and 35 Indian boats and 194 crew. It has been decided to release them by July 15, 1997," the statement said.
"It has also been decided that other boats and crew will be released as and when identified," it added.

Pakistan said in March it was ready to free 38 Indian children held with adult fishermen as a unilateral goodwill gesture before the first round of talks between top Indian and Pakistani foreign ministry officials in New Delhi.
Monday's statement was issued after a second round of talks in Islamabad, in which the two sides set an agenda for future peace talks and agreed on a negotiating mechanism.
